**// IMPORTANT & REQUIRE YOUR SUPPORT //**

TO : BUREAU VERITAS(BV)

TO : EUNSUNG HEAVY INDUSTRIES / Mr. IC Kim

TO : JUNGHAE ENGINEERING / Mr. JH Park

FM : K-WIND SOLUTION CO., LTD. / as owner’s representative

--------------------------------

Dear Sirs.

Good day.

This CTV which will be built for the first time in Korea with the active technical support of you class BV and the dedicated cooperation of the field inspector of the BV Korea branch is currently about to be completed.

Currently field inspectors at BV Korea branch provide careful inspection and technical advice at all stages of the construction process which is essential support for the successful completion of this CTV.

As is well known this first CTV currently under construction began full-scale production with STEEL CUTTING in November last year. However, the Launching schedule, which was originally scheduled for the End of June, was postponed once to the End of July, and recently it was postponed again to 18TH Aug.. Also, the ship delivery date of CTV was notified by the shipyard as End of Aug..

This delay in shipbuilding has led to an increase in labor costs at the shipyard and a delay in the chartering business of the shipowner, and the damage is much greater than expected. In particular, economic losses are seriously affecting the overall profitability of the project beyond a simple delay.

What is more problematic is that some of the attached BV comments were presented by the BV after the hull construction work has already been completed. These include the parts that are practically difficult to re-construct. This situation is due to some errors due to long distance management between Singapore approval department and actual site progress, and the errors to timely check the site situation, and various outstanding situations are mixed.

Comments on areas where hull construction has already been completed and cannot be re-constructed are requested that if the area has no problem with vessel service strength, please file close early or reply with BV’s technical instruction to the design company(architect) and shipyard as soon as possible. This is a major concern for the shipowner and needs to be processed quickly to prevent further delays.

We sincerely ask for active cooperation and thorough on-site supervision from you class BV to prevent further disruptions to the Launch date and delivery schedule currently scheduled for 18TH Aug..

In particular, it is very important for ships to be delivered in a timely manner according to the contract schedule between the ship owner and the charterer. Delays in ship delivery can lead to a variety of legal and economic problems, such as contractual penalties and loss of business opportunities.

Therefore, we ask for your cooperation to facilitate the remaining process through BV's proactive on-site supervision and rapid technical decision. In particular, we ask you to minimize unnecessary rework on the already completed process and actively consider practical alternatives to the extent that there are no safety problems.

We look forward to the active cooperation and support of all concerned so that the remaining schedule can proceed smoothly.

Thank you.
